MY.note: TNB Ultra-High-Voltage DC class (>100MW), RP4 Jul 2025; base industrial ~0.11. Sarawak (SESCO hydro) cheaper.

SG.note: Contestable-market estimate for large DCs (0.17-0.22); SP regulated tariff ~0.25 Q3 2026.

ID.note: PLN B-3/I-3 (medium-voltage, >200kVA) Rp1,122/kWh @ ~Rp18,100/USD; frozen ~10yrs. Hyperscale on I-4 (>=30MVA) ~Rp997 = $0.055; negotiated 'Layanan Khusus' premium service ~Rp1,645 = $0.091. REC green premium +Rp35/kWh. NOTE: PLN Batam is a SEPARATE island grid (unsubsidised, DC rates negotiated and unpublished) — treat Batam facilities as unknown-but-competitive vs SG/Johor.

TH.note: MEA/PEA Type 4.2 large-industrial TOU (>=69kV), ERC May-Aug 2026: 4.10 on-peak / 2.58 off-peak THB/kWh + Ft 0.1623 + demand charge; blended for 24/7 DC load ~3.4 THB/kWh @ 33.3 THB/USD. Utility Green Tariff UGT2 (the DC product, live 2026) ~4.55 THB/kWh = ~$0.137 — green power in TH costs more than Malaysia's grey grid. Govt target of 2.5 THB/kWh (~$0.075) for DCs not yet delivered.

VN.note: EVN production/manufacturing tariff, >=110kV, Decision 1279/QD-BCT (eff 10 May 2025): 1,811 normal / 1,146 off-peak / 3,266 peak VND/kWh, blended 24/7 across the Decision 963/QD-BCT TOU windows (eff 22 Apr 2026; off-peak 42h/wk, peak 30h/wk Mon-Sat, normal 96h/wk) = 1,905 VND/kWh @ 26,268 VND/USD, ex-VAT. *** CLASSIFICATION IS CONTESTED — THIS IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE RISK IN THE VN DATA. *** Circular 60/2025/TT-BCT (eff 2 Dec 2025), Article 11(19), created a BUSINESS-tariff category for 'facilities providing centralised data processing, storage and management services', and EVN duly billed data centres at business rates from Dec 2025 (CMC reported a >50% jump across its first three invoices; Viettel/VNPT/FPT/CMC/VNG filed a joint petition). MOIT initially DEFENDED that reading (18 Feb 2026). After a Ministry of Science & Technology opinion (9 Apr 2026) that a DC's technical system is a production activity, an MOIT letter (cong van) to EVN (~4 May 2026) directed that where buyer and seller cannot agree a use-purpose split — which is infeasible inside a DC — the DC's TECHNICAL SYSTEM takes the PRODUCTION tariff. So production is correct in practice today. BUT THE REVERSAL IS AN ADMINISTRATIVE LETTER, NOT AN AMENDMENT: Art. 11(19) is STILL IN FORCE, and the draft TT60 amendment (28 May 2026) does not touch it. Stable in practice, unstable on paper — one clause deletion or one contrary letter flips it. DOWNSIDE CASE: the business class has NO >=110kV band (top band is '22kV and above': 2,887/1,609/5,025 VND normal/off-peak/peak), so a 110kV DC would get no HV discount at all and blends to ~US$0.112/kWh — **+55%, or ~US$28M/yr extra on a 100MW site at 80% utilisation**. Also note: the widely-quoted 'Vietnam $0.085/kWh' is EVN's ALL-CUSTOMER average retail price (2,204 VND/kWh), not the HV industrial class. Price is on an escalator (+4.8% Oct 2024, +4.8% May 2025) and Decree 278/2026 (eff 9 Jul 2026) lets EVN re-price QUARTERLY. No DC-specific tariff class exists. No DC has signed a DPPA (the first live one, Jun 2026, is Samsung — a manufacturer). The real VN constraint remains power DELIVERY, not price: C&W puts a new 100MW connection at 2-3 years.

PH.note: NOT the regulated Meralco tariff - any DC-scale load is a Contestable Customer under RCOA/Open Access (threshold cut 500kW -> 100kW on 26 Jun 2026) and buys generation from a Retail Electricity Supplier. Meralco's own hyperscale white paper (7 Jul 2025, using ERC CREM/GEOP Feb-2025 data, load factor 0.95, 10-100MW 24/7 profile): standard RCOA all-in US$0.121/kWh ex-tax (gen PHP 5.50-6.00 + NGCP transmission + Meralco distribution + universal charges); optimised bilateral RCOA US$0.110. Central 0.12, band 0.10-0.13. CREATE MORE (200% power-cost deduction, zero-rated VAT for export-registered locators) takes the effective rate to ~$0.10. The captive/regulated route is far worse (~PHP 9.2/kWh ex-VAT = ~$0.15 on the Feb-2026 GP 115kV Very-Large schedule) but no DC pays it. The headline 'PHP 14.83/kWh' (Jul 2026) is RESIDENTIAL = ~$0.24/kWh: Philippine households pay Singapore prices while a contestable DC pays half. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE COMMON NARRATIVE: PH is NO LONGER the most expensive DC power in SEA - at $0.12 it now sits BELOW Malaysia ($0.14, post-RP4) and Singapore ($0.20), roughly at Thailand. Deregulation is a DISCOUNT for big loads, not a penalty. The binding PH constraint is grid RELIABILITY and carbon (Luzon red-alerted 14-15 May 2026 with 4,242MW on forced outage; >60% coal; Malampaya gas depleting ~2030), not price. WEAKEST LINK: the RCOA generation price is ERC data from Feb 2025, 17 months stale - refresh from ERC's monthly CREM/GEOP statistics.

AE.note: STILL NULL AS ONE COUNTRY FIGURE, BUT BOTH EMIRATES ARE NOW VERIFIED AGAINST PRIMARY SCHEDULES (2026-08-28), AND THE EARLIER SECONDARY FIGURES WERE BOTH WRONG. DUBAI (DEWA, dewa.gov.ae slab tariff page, fuel surcharge line dated August 2026): the industrial slab is AED 0.230/kWh only for the first 10,000 kWh per month and AED 0.380/kWh above it. A data centre passes 10,000 kWh in under an hour, so it sits entirely in the upper band. With the August 2026 fuel surcharge of AED 0.060/kWh and 5% VAT, the all-in rate is AED 0.462/kWh, about US$0.126/kWh. The AED 0.230 figure that circulates is the bottom slab and is irrelevant to a data centre. ABU DHABI (ADDC / TAQA Distribution published schedule): the correct class is Industry, more than 1 MW, at 27 fils/kWh (AED 0.270) for most hours and 36.6 fils/kWh (AED 0.366) at peak, which is 10am to 10pm from 1 June to 30 September only. Rates appear VAT-inclusive. That is about US$0.074/kWh off-peak. The AED 0.150 figure that circulates does not match the official schedule. THIS INVERTS THE COMMON CLAIM THAT GULF POWER IS CHEAP. At about US$0.126/kWh Dubai would be the most expensive market in this entire dataset, above the Philippines at US$0.12. Abu Dhabi at about US$0.074 sits near Vietnam, the cheapest market in Southeast Asia. The two emirates differ by roughly 70%, so a single AE figure would be wrong on its face and the field stays null. Handle per market, not per country. STILL UNPUBLISHED: Abu Dhabi's Department of Energy confirmed on the record (World Future Energy Summit, Jan 2026) that it is designing a dedicated cost-reflective hyperscaler tariff, with no rate and no launch date announced. Bespoke non-standard rates for the largest customers are also unpublished, so what a hyperscale campus actually pays may differ from both figures above.

SA.note: STILL NULL AND STILL UNVERIFIED after a dedicated primary-source attempt on 2026-08-28. SERA's own tariff pages are JavaScript-driven and returned no readable content, and archive access was unavailable. Secondary sources actively conflict with each other on both bands, giving the commercial threshold rate as SAR 0.18, 0.20 and 0.22/kWh and the upper band as SAR 0.30 or 0.32. That spread is not reconcilable without the primary schedule. A STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE RATE: SERA's Grid Code refers to an Eligible Consumer status tied to contracted load, which is the likely mechanism for a large directly connected campus to sit outside the retail tariff table entirely on bilateral terms. That mirrors Abu Dhabi's unpublished non-standard rates, and it means the published brackets may be the wrong question. Which class a hyperscale campus falls into remains unresolved. NO PRICED DATA-CENTRE PPA EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE GULF. The low Saudi renewable prices that circulate (Sudair, Dawadmi at about US$0.0133/kWh, Bisha, Humaij, Khulis at roughly 1.3 US cents) are all national-grid procurements by the Principal Buyer and none names a data centre as offtaker. DataVolt's NEOM campus has no disclosed price.

IN.note: DELIBERATELY NULL. Electricity tariffs in India are set by each state regulator, so a single country figure would be wrong on its face, the same reason AE is null. Handle per market. HT industrial energy charges found on 2026-09-27 (INR/kWh, FY2025-26, before demand charges, duties and cross-subsidy surcharge): Maharashtra MSEDCL 7.48 plus 0.62 wheeling with a 10% wheeling discount for data centres; Tamil Nadu TANGEDCO 7.50; Telangana TGSPDCL 7.65, 7.15 or 6.65 by voltage; Uttar Pradesh HV-2 7.97 with a data-centre demand charge of Rs 270/kVA under the NIDP order (the only state with a data-centre tariff class); Karnataka HT-2(a) 6.70 (order of 3 Mar 2026); West Bengal 6.87 to 6.91 at 33kV. At about 86 INR/USD these span roughly US$0.078 to 0.093/kWh. Large campuses increasingly run on captive or open-access renewables (Reliance Jamnagar, Digital Edge 83MW solar PPA), so the grid tariff is an upper bound for them.

QA.note: NULL PENDING A PRIMARY READ. Kahramaa publishes a flat non-residential rate rather than an industrial band; a secondary source records QAR 0.130/kWh (about US$0.036) as of March 2025 citing Kahramaa. Kahramaa's own page (km.qa) was not reached. Enter only after reading it.

BH.note: EWA published non-domestic tariff (ewa.bh/en/tariff): 22 fils/kWh up to 5,000 kWh a month and 32 fils/kWh above. A data centre passes the slab in the first hours of a month, so 32 fils (about US$0.085) is the working rate. No industrial class exists. Any bilateral large-user rate is unpublished.

CN.note: DELIBERATELY NULL. No national data centre tariff exists and prices vary by province. Zhongwei data centres pay a delivered price of 0.36 yuan/kWh under the green power park's market mechanism (Economic Daily, 2026-04-23, http://paper.ce.cn/pad/content/202604/23/content_331502.html; China Daily 2026-06-05 for China Mobile Park B). That is a negotiated outcome, not a published regulated tariff, and is not converted to US dollars here. The Ningxia large-industry catalogue tariff was not found in an allowed source.

Johor.vacancy_basis: 'Colocation Vacancy' %, C&W primary-market table, sits alongside operational capacity of 897MW. Denominator unit (MW IT load vs white space vs racks) not stated in the free source; label implies colocation stock only. [refresh 2026-08-28] C&W H1 2026 carries Johor unchanged at 0.7%, with combined operational plus future capacity still above 4GW and the widest lead in Asia Pacific.
Johor.prelease_note: No market-wide pre-lease rate is published for Johor. Operator-level datapoint only: AirTrunk states JHB1 + JHB2 (together >420MW IT load) are 'almost 100% contracted and tracking well ahead of investment plans' (AirTrunk press statement accompanying the JHB3/JHB4 announcement, May 2026). This is two campuses, not the market. Knight Frank's separate framing, Johor '99% taken up', is a restatement of the 1.1% vacancy on OPERATIONAL stock, not a pre-lease rate on under-construction stock; do not read it as a pipeline pre-commitment figure.
Johor.market_definition_note: C&W and Knight Frank both treat 'Johor' as a single metro/state market. Knight Frank's Johor commentary references land in 'major tech parks' and the Sedenak/Kulai-anchored build-out, and C&W's Johor pipeline (315MW U/C, 2,099MW planned) is only reconcilable with a state-wide footprint. So Johor almost certainly = our Johor (Kulai/Sedenak/Iskandar Puteri/JB), but neither source publishes an explicit sub-district boundary list. Match: HIGH confidence, not explicitly stated.
Johor.operational_note: Colocation only. Unit not stated by the source.

Klang Valley.market_definition_note: NO PUBLISHED VACANCY RATE. C&W's APAC report names Johor as Malaysia's only primary market and its six secondary markets are Delhi, Taipei, Auckland, Manila, Ho Chi Minh City and Perth, Klang Valley/KL is not covered. Knight Frank's APAC DC report covers Johor, not KL. Structure Research publishes a 'Kuala Lumpur DCAI Report 2025' (allowed source) but the public press release discloses only market value (US$300m in 2025, 31% CAGR to $1.1bn by 2030), no vacancy or utilisation. JLL Malaysia has published Greater KL CAPACITY only (182MW completed, 615MW under construction, 765MW pipeline; Cyberjaya / Bukit Jalil / Petaling Jaya / KL city / northern KL), no vacancy. Any Klang Valley vacancy number would have to be bought (Structure Research / DC Byte), do not synthesise one.

Singapore.vacancy_basis: 'Colocation Vacancy' %, C&W primary-market table, alongside 1,043MW operational / 20MW U/C / 237MW planned. Denominator unit not stated in the free source. [refresh 2026-08-28] C&W published an H1 2026 edition but its Singapore and Jakarta percentages are behind the report paywall and were not obtainable. The figure here stays at the Dec-2025 vintage. THE VINTAGE GAP HAS MOVED TO THIS MARKET. Manila, Bangkok and HCMC are now H1 2026 while this one is six months older.
Singapore.prelease_note: No pre-lease percentage published for Singapore's under-construction stock, and with only 20MW under construction (C&W, H2 2025) the metric is near-meaningless here. The binding mechanism is regulatory allocation, not leasing: IMDA/EDB's second Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA2, launched 2025-12-01) allocates 'at least 200MW'; applications closed 2026-03-31, delivery 2026-2028. The 2023 pilot allocated 80MW to Equinix, GDS, Microsoft and an AirTrunk/ByteDance consortium. Capacity in Singapore is effectively spoken-for before it is built, but no operator or broker publishes a % pre-let.
Singapore.market_definition_note: Singapore = the whole city-state in every source. Perfect match to our market. No definitional risk.
Singapore.operational_note: Colocation only. Unit not stated by the source.

Greater Jakarta.vacancy_basis: 'Colocation Vacancy' %, C&W primary-market table, alongside 322MW operational / 186MW U/C / 901MW planned. Denominator unit not stated in the free source. [refresh 2026-08-28] C&W published an H1 2026 edition but its Singapore and Jakarta percentages are behind the report paywall and were not obtainable. The figure here stays at the Dec-2025 vintage. THE VINTAGE GAP HAS MOVED TO THIS MARKET. Manila, Bangkok and HCMC are now H1 2026 while this one is six months older.
Greater Jakarta.prelease_note: Not published. No operator or broker gives a pre-commitment rate on Jakarta's 186MW under construction. Given a 24.9% vacancy on existing stock, absence of a pre-lease number is itself informative, nobody is advertising one.
Greater Jakarta.market_definition_note: C&W's 'Greater Jakarta' explicitly includes Cikarang, C&W states Cikarang accounts for ~47% of Jakarta's operational capacity and 61% of its development pipeline. So the Bekasi/Cikarang corridor IS in the denominator, matching our market. Whether Karawang, Bogor and Tangerang are also included is NOT stated. Match: GOOD on the Cikarang/Bekasi core, UNVERIFIED on the outer ring.
Greater Jakarta.operational_note: Colocation only, includes Cikarang. Unit not stated by the source.

Bangkok metro.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy %, C&W Asia Pacific Data Centre Update H1 2026, reported 2026-08-26. Rose from 17.6% at Dec 2025, a real 4.5-point move. Bangkok under-construction capacity rose 148% to 859MW in H1 2026, one of the fastest builds in Asia Pacific, so the rising vacancy reads as new supply landing ahead of demand rather than demand weakening. Denominator unit is not stated in the free source. The C&W market boundary for 'Bangkok' is still unpublished, so it may or may not include the EEC. Do not apply it to our Bangkok-metro entries alone without flagging.
Bangkok metro.prelease_note: Not published. Bangkok has 347MW under construction against a 113MW operational base, a 3x build on a small base, and no operator or broker discloses how much of it is pre-let. This is the single biggest information gap in the set given the size of the TH pipeline.
Bangkok metro.market_definition_note: RISK: C&W calls the market 'Bangkok' and does not publish its boundary. It is NOT stated whether Chonburi / Rayong / Chachoengsao (the EEC) sit inside 'Bangkok' or outside it. Given the 113MW operational figure is small relative to Thailand's total, and several of the largest TH projects (e.g. EEC-located hyperscale campuses) are still under construction, the 347MW U/C figure may or may not include EEC sites. Our Bangkok-metro vs EEC split may therefore NOT be reconcilable with C&W's single 'Bangkok' number. Treat 17.6% as 'Thailand's primary DC market as C&W defines it', and do not apply it to our Bangkok-metro entries alone without flagging.
Bangkok metro.operational_note: Colocation only. Whether the Eastern Seaboard is included is not published. Vintage approximate.

Penang / North MY.market_definition_note: NO PUBLISHED VACANCY RATE. Not tracked as a market by C&W, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Structure Research. Only appears in banned-aggregator portfolio databases (Arizton/R&M), which give facility counts, not vacancy.

Sarawak & E. Malaysia.market_definition_note: NO PUBLISHED VACANCY RATE. Same as Penang/Kedah, below every brokerage's market-coverage threshold.

EEC (Eastern Seaboard).market_definition_note: NO SEPARATE PUBLISHED VACANCY RATE. No brokerage treats Chonburi/Rayong/Chachoengsao as a standalone market. It is either folded into C&W's 'Bangkok' (unstated) or not covered. Structure Research's Bangkok report (released Q4 2025) may resolve the boundary but its public material discloses only market value (2024: ~US$165m, ~56MW built-out; forecast US$540m by 2029), no vacancy.

Greater Manila.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy as a share of operational capacity. C&W Asia Pacific Data Centre Update H1 2026, reported by BusinessWorld on 2026-08-26. Manila operational capacity is 90MW across 28 facilities run by 16 operators, up 22% half-on-half. Pipeline is 97MW (5MW under construction, 92MW planned), down 13% as completions outpaced new announcements. THE VINTAGE GAP IS CLOSED. This replaces the Jun-2025 44.0% figure that could not be rolled forward. Vacancy fell only 4.4 points while operational capacity grew 22%, so absorption is real but still lagging supply. READ THE NUMBER CORRECTLY. This is absorption lag, a third distinct cause alongside demand-tight (Johor 0.7%) and policy-tight (Singapore 4.9%).
Greater Manila.market_definition_note: NCR + the CALABARZON ring (Cavite / Laguna / Batangas) as ONE market, because that is how C&W measures it, its 'Manila' section covers both Equinix MN1-3 inside NCR and Digital Edge NARRA1 at Laguna Technopark. Boundary is INFERRED FROM ASSET COVERAGE, not an explicit C&W definition. Internally the two halves do behave differently (NCR = interconnection/IX market, small sites, all four Manila internet exchanges; CALABARZON = the hyperscale land+MW belt inside PEZA ecozones, home to VITRO Sta. Rosa and VITRO General Trias), but they are kept together so the published vacancy denominator stays intact. READ THE 44% CORRECTLY: it is ABSORPTION LAG, not disinterest, operational capacity jumped 31% in six months and C&W expects the rate to ease as the new stock leases up. That is a THIRD distinct cause of a vacancy reading, alongside demand-tight (Johor 0.7%) and policy-tight (Singapore 4.9%).
Greater Manila.operational_note: Colocation only, 28 facilities, includes the Cavite and Laguna ring.

HCMC metro.vacancy_basis: FIRST EVER PUBLISHED HCMC VACANCY FIGURE. C&W Asia Pacific Data Centre Update H1 2026 covers HCMC as a secondary market and for the first time carries a percentage, where every prior edition was qualitative only. 34.8% vacancy against 33MW of live IT capacity across 14 facilities run by 9 operators, plus 68MW of future supply (14MW under construction, 54MW in investment preparation). Basis is explicitly IT capacity, the same basis we use. Reported via Tuoi Tre News 2026-08-05 and BusinessWorld 2026-08-26; the C&W report itself is gated. The 33MW live figure sits close to our own disclosed HCMC total, which corroborates the market split. Hanoi remains uncovered and is reported only inside C&W's emerging-markets aggregate.
HCMC metro.market_definition_note: HCMC + the southern industrial belt (Cu Chi / Tan Phu Trung, Saigon Hi-Tech Park in Thu Duc, Tan Thuan EPZ, VSIP III in Binh Duong). Distinct on all three inputs: the southern 500kV ring and Vietnam's solar/wind fleet are HERE while the load is in the north (the N-S 500kV corridor is the national bottleneck); land sits in established hi-tech/export parks; and demand is private/foreign rather than state. 10 of 18 VN entries and EVERY VN project >=100MW are in this market. C&W puts HCMC at roughly half of national live capacity.

Hanoi metro.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. Hanoi is not a C&W market at all, not primary, not one of the six secondary markets (Delhi, Taipei, Auckland, Manila, HCMC, Perth). It appears only as a name inside the 30-market Maturity Index with no stat block. No third party publishes a Hanoi vacancy rate.
Hanoi metro.market_definition_note: Hanoi + Hoa Lac Hi-Tech Park (Thach That) + the northern industrial belt (Bac Ninh, Hung Yen, Bac Giang). This is the STATE/SOE market: Viettel, VNPT, the Ministry of Public Security's National Data Center No.1 and the FPT-Nvidia AI factory all sit here, and demand is government + domestic telco rather than foreign colo. It also carries Vietnam's grid risk, the Jun 2023 rolling blackouts hit exactly these industrial parks (Samsung, Foxconn, Canon, Luxshare) at a cost of ~US$1.4bn (World Bank), because generation is in the south and centre while load is in the north.

Clark / Central Luzon.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No third party publishes a vacancy series for Central Luzon.
Clark / Central Luzon.market_definition_note: Clark Freeport / New Clark City / Angeles / Tarlac / Pampanga (Region III). The government's designated overflow metro: its own airport, its own freeport incentives, and pitched as seismically and flood-safer than the NCR. CRITICAL POWER CAVEAT: parts of Central Luzon sit OUTSIDE the Meralco franchise, so a project here cannot lean on Meralco's 115kV network plan, the 300MW Narra Technology Park (New Clark City) is the clearest case, and its lack of any named utility partner is a large part of why we hold it at land_permitting.

Da Nang / Central VN.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. Not tracked as a market by any third party.
Da Nang / Central VN.market_definition_note: Da Nang + the central coast. A SUBSEA-CABLE market, not a demand market: Da Nang is Vietnam's cable-landing cluster (APG, AAE-1, SMW-3, plus the new ADC/SJC2 systems), so it sells latency and international transit rather than local load, the VN analogue of Batam, which sells latency to Singapore. Da Nang also hosts Vietnam's free-trade/AI-zone policy pilot. Both entries here are small (10MW-class) and early; nothing has crossed the 20MW bar on its own merits.

Other Indonesia.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED, residual bucket, not a measured market.
Other Indonesia.market_definition_note: Residual bucket: Indonesian facilities outside Greater Jakarta and Batam-Bintan (Surabaya, Solo, Bali, Kalimantan). Not a single catchment and no third party publishes metrics for it, it exists so country totals reconcile.

Other Thailand.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED, residual bucket, not a measured market.
Other Thailand.market_definition_note: Residual bucket: Thai facilities outside Bangkok metro and the EEC. Not a single catchment and no third party publishes metrics for it, it exists so country totals reconcile.

Abu Dhabi.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
Abu Dhabi.market_definition_note: The sovereign AI campus market. G42 and its subsidiaries Khazna and Core42 dominate, and the sites are government-adjacent and very large. KEZAD, Masdar City, Mafraq, Yas Island and the Stargate UAE campus all sit here. Structurally different from Dubai on every input, since capital is sovereign, tenants are US hyperscalers and AI labs, and chip access runs through named entities on a US approved list. NO PUBLISHER MEASURES ABU DHABI AND DUBAI AS ONE MARKET OR AS TWO, because no vacancy series exists for either. The split here is ours, made on how the markets actually behave, and it should be revisited the moment anyone publishes a figure.

Dubai.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
Dubai.market_definition_note: The diversified and connectivity-led market. A broader operator base than Abu Dhabi, including du and Datamena, Equinix, Gulf Data Hub and Moro Hub, with a telco, interconnection and enterprise character. Dubai Silicon Oasis, Dubai South, Dubai Production City and the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park are the clusters. DEWA tariffs are materially higher than Abu Dhabi's, which is itself a reason to keep the two apart.

Northern Emirates.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. Northern Emirates.market_definition_note: Ajman, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Thin today and it exists as a row for one reason, which is that Khazna's QAJ1 in Ajman is a 100MW IT-load facility with Microsoft as a confirmed anchor tenant. That is the largest explicitly IT-load-stated figure found anywhere in the UAE, so folding it into Dubai would misplace it.

Riyadh.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
Riyadh.market_definition_note: The largest Saudi market by facility count and the centre of the national AI programme. Humain's flagship campus, the SDAIA Hexagon government facility, most of stc and center3, the Alibaba and stc SCCC joint venture, Zain, Ezditek and the DataVolt East Riyadh site. Also home to Humain's Al-Saad site, a 24 square kilometre landholding whose 6,000MW figure is a masterplan ceiling with only electrical infrastructure out to tender.

Dammam / Eastern Province.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
Dammam / Eastern Province.market_definition_note: The industrial-anchor market and, on at least one third-party count, the leader on live capacity even though Riyadh leads on facility count. Aramco and Aramco Digital, the Google Cloud region built with Aramco, the Groq inference deployment, EDGNEX Dammam, Humain's second campus and Khazna's Saudi land. Its character is heavy industry and enterprise rather than the sovereign AI programme, which is why it is kept apart from Riyadh.

Jeddah / Western.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
Jeddah / Western.market_definition_note: The smaller telecom and colocation market on the Red Sea coast. center3's Jeddah203, Oracle's original 2020 Saudi region, and part of Alfanar's four-site plan. Its distinguishing asset is subsea landing, since it is the gateway for the 2Africa cable and the JEDIX internet exchange, which makes it Saudi Arabia's connectivity market rather than a demand market.

NEOM / Oxagon.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No colocation vacancy percentage for any Gulf market was found from Cushman & Wakefield, Knight Frank, CBRE, JLL or Savills. This is a genuine gap in the published record rather than a search failure, and it is a real difference from Southeast Asia where five markets carry a figure. Do not estimate one.
NEOM / Oxagon.market_definition_note: A greenfield market with almost nothing built. DataVolt's Oxagon campus is the only significant project and its first 300MW phase is not targeted before 2028, against a 1,500MW full-build ceiling. Powered by NEOM's own wind and solar rather than the national grid, so its power economics are not comparable to the other three Saudi markets and its numbers should never be blended with them.

Batam and Bintan.market_definition_note: NO PUBLISHED VACANCY RATE. Batam is named by CBRE (Global DC Trends 2026) as an emerging market 'gaining traction by offering scalable land and power availability' and by Knight Frank as absorbing Singapore overflow alongside Johor, but neither publishes a vacancy, take-up or pre-lease figure for it. It is not a primary or secondary market in C&W's APAC report. Bintan is not tracked by anyone.

Mumbai metro.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026 puts Mumbai at 890MW operational and 1,726MW pipeline, more than half of India.
Mumbai metro.market_definition_note: Mumbai Metropolitan Region including Navi Mumbai (Airoli, Mahape, Rabale, Turbhe), Panvel and Taloja, Thane and Kalyan-Dombivli (Palava), and provisionally Raigad (AirTrunk Pen). Split Taloja or Raigad out the way the state reports them if either grows into its own cluster.

Pune.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 133MW operational, 258MW pipeline.
Pune.market_definition_note: Pune district, including Hinjewadi, Talegaon, Chakan and Dighi.

Chennai.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 214MW operational, 368MW pipeline. Absorption-lag reading, new stock leasing up.
Chennai.market_definition_note: Chennai metropolitan area, chiefly Ambattur and the Siruseri/OMR corridor, plus Sriperumbudur and Oragadam.

Hyderabad.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 151MW operational, 710MW pipeline. Excludes hyperscaler self-build, which is most of Hyderabad.
Hyderabad.market_definition_note: Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy district, including Gachibowli, Shamshabad, Chandanvelly, Mekaguda, Elikatta and Bharat Future City. Hyperscaler self-build (Microsoft, AWS) dominates and sits outside the vacancy denominator.

Bengaluru.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 162MW operational, 100MW pipeline. Absorption-lag reading.
Bengaluru.market_definition_note: Bengaluru urban, including Whitefield, Electronic City and Devanahalli.

NCR.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 183MW operational, 387MW pipeline. Absorption-lag reading in the Manila sense, not a demand failure.
NCR.market_definition_note: National Capital Region as C&W measures it (Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Gurugram, Manesar) plus Panchkula and Rai in Haryana, which sell into NCR demand. C&W excludes Panchkula; the difference is small today.

Kolkata.vacancy_basis: Colocation vacancy by city from Cushman & Wakefield's India Data Centre Update H1 2025 (data as of Jun 2025). The H1 2026 update (23 Sep 2026) publishes a national colo vacancy of 14.9% and city operational MW, with city vacancy inside the full PDF that was not read; never roll the H1 2025 figure forward and show the vintage gap. C&W is the only broker publishing city vacancy for India; JLL and CBRE publish capacity and absorption only. C&W H1 2026: 22MW operational, 84MW pipeline, which is incompatible with every announced Kolkata campus being live and is why live MW stays null on those rows.
Kolkata.market_definition_note: Kolkata metropolitan area, chiefly New Town/Rajarhat (Bengal Silicon Valley) and Uttarpara.

Visakhapatnam.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No broker measures Visakhapatnam as a market. The pipeline here is hyperscaler self-build and sovereign programme capacity.
Visakhapatnam.market_definition_note: Visakhapatnam and its northern suburbs (Madhurawada, Rushikonda, Paradesipalem). Exists as a market because of the Google, Adani and Airtel AI hub and Sify.

Gujarat.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No broker vacancy series for Gujarat.
Gujarat.market_definition_note: Jamnagar (Reliance) and GIFT City/Ahmedabad and Dholera if anything crosses the bar. Jamnagar runs on Reliance captive renewables and its economics are not comparable to grid-fed markets.

Other India.market_definition_note: Single sites outside the seven measured cities and the two hubs above (Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh outside NCR, Rajasthan).

Doha.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No C&W, JLL, Knight Frank or CBRE vacancy series for Doha. Do not estimate one.
Doha.market_definition_note: Qatar as one market. Meeza is most of it; Syntys (Ooredoo carve-out) holds the rest.

Manama.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No broker vacancy series for Bahrain. Do not estimate one.
Manama.market_definition_note: Bahrain as one market. center3 Bahrain Data Center Park and the AWS me-south-1 region (on hold after the 2026 strikes).

Zhongwei.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED as vacancy. Economic Daily (2026-02-08) reports a cluster rack utilisation rate (上架率) above 80%, which measures racks in use, not leasable capacity sitting empty. Do not convert it into vacancy.
Zhongwei.market_definition_note: Zhongwei data centre cluster in Ningxia, one of the national East Data West Computing hubs, mostly within the Zhongwei cloud base and the newer Xuanhe area. Fed by green power under a direct supply scheme, so its power economics are not comparable to grid-fed markets.

Kuwait.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No broker vacancy series for Kuwait. Do not estimate one.
Kuwait.market_definition_note: Kuwait as one market. Google Cloud's three-site region is the only row.

Horinger and Hohhot.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Horinger and Hohhot.market_definition_note: Horinger cluster south of Hohhot, the Inner Mongolia national computing hub. Officials reported 532,000 standard racks in use across 57 projects in June 2026. Power is largely wind and solar over private lines at about 0.32 to 0.36 yuan per kWh as reported.

Ulanqab.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Ulanqab.market_definition_note: Ulanqab cluster in Inner Mongolia, about 150 km east of Hohhot, mostly the Jining, Yiwutang and Bayin parks. The city reported about 500,000 racks built and 330,000 operating in June 2026. Power is largely wind and solar over private lines.

Qingyang.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Qingyang.market_definition_note: Qingyang cluster in Gansu, centred on the East Data West Computing industrial park in Xifeng district. Officials reported more than 102,000 standard racks built by May 2026. A 2GW wind and solar aggregation pilot by Gansu Electric Power Investment supplies part of park demand.

Gui'an.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Gui'an.market_definition_note: Gui'an cluster in Guizhou, the Guizhou national computing hub, mostly in Gui'an New Area. Guiyang Daily (Aug 2025) counts 26 large centres with 161,800 standard racks powered. It runs on the Guizhou provincial grid.

Shaoguan.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Shaoguan.market_definition_note: Shaoguan cluster in northern Guangdong, the Greater Bay Area national hub node, unveiled on 29 May 2022 with a 6,277 mu start-up zone. Officials reported six projects operating with about 173,000 standard racks and about 145,000 more under construction in Jun 2026.

Tianfu (Chengdu).vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Tianfu (Chengdu).market_definition_note: Tianfu cluster in Sichuan, the Chengdu half of the Chengdu-Chongqing national hub, covering Tianfu New Area, Chengdu Eastern New Area, the High-tech Zone, Shuangliu, Pidu and Jianyang. Sichuan reported 84,000 standard racks built in 2023.

Chongqing.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Chongqing.market_definition_note: Chongqing cluster, the Chongqing half of the Chengdu-Chongqing national hub, centred on the Shuitu International Data Port in Liangjiang New Area, with Western (Chongqing) Science City and the Economic and Technological Development Zone as newer sites. Shuitu hosted 10 large data centres with 32,000 racks in May 2024.

Wuhu.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Wuhu.market_definition_note: The Wuhu data centre cluster is one of two national clusters in the Yangtze River Delta hub of the East Data West Computing plan, approved in 2022. Its start-up zone centres on the Zhonghua Shudao (中华数岛) area north of the Yangtze in Wuhu, Anhui. Wuhu reported 224,700 standard racks built and 64,000P of AI compute as of Jul 2026 (Science and Technology Daily, 6 Aug 2026).

Qingpu-Wujiang-Jiashan.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Qingpu-Wujiang-Jiashan.market_definition_note: The Yangtze River Delta Ecological Green Integration Demonstration Zone cluster is the second national cluster in the Yangtze River Delta hub. Its start-up area is Qingpu District in Shanghai, Wujiang District in Suzhou and Jiashan County in Jiaxing. The 2022 plan requires average rack utilisation of at least 65% and PUE within 1.25 (Qingpu District Government, 21 Feb 2022).

Zhangjiakou.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Zhangjiakou.market_definition_note: The Zhangjiakou data centre cluster is the Hebei part of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei national computing hub. It spans Zhangbei, Xuanhua, Huailai and the city districts. Xinhua reported 49 data centres built and 810,000 standard racks in operation (Apr 2026), and Hebei Daily counted 53 operating computing centres at end-June 2026. This market covers Zhangbei, Xuanhua, Yuxian and the city, with Huailai tracked separately.

Huailai.vacancy_basis: NOT PUBLISHED. No vacancy figure exists for this cluster. Rack utilisation (上架率), where reported, measures racks in use and is never converted into vacancy.
Huailai.market_definition_note: Huailai County sits next to Beijing's Yanqing district and is the densest part of the Zhangjiakou cluster. Chindata, Hoyinn, China Unicom, China Telecom, Tencent, CapitalOnline and Aofei all build here. Hoyinn alone runs 700 MW IT and Chindata nearly 500 MW (2025-2026 sources). The Huailai Big Data Industrial Base was named a national new industrialisation demonstration base (Nov 2024).

meta.markets_note: FIVE of our 14 markets have a published, dated, market-level colocation vacancy rate. FOUR come from Cushman & Wakefield's APAC Data Centre Update H2 2025 (data as of Dec 2025, published 27 Mar 2026): Johor 0.7%, Singapore 4.9% (CBRE says 2.0%, both carried, never averaged), Bangkok 17.6%, Greater Jakarta 24.9% (trend 36→31→24.9 across 2025 = demand eating a flat supply base). The FIFTH, Greater Manila 44.0%, comes from C&W's APAC Data Centre Update H1 2025 and is JUN-2025 DATA, six months staler than the other four. C&W has published no H2 2025 Manila figure; it must not be rolled forward, and the vintage gap must be shown wherever the number is. NO THIRD PARTY PUBLISHES A VACANCY RATE FOR HCMC, HANOI, KLANG VALLEY, BATAM, EEC, PENANG, SARAWAK OR CLARK, those are left blank and are NEVER estimated. (Hanoi is not even a C&W market; HCMC is covered only qualitatively.) Vacancy = built, leasable COLO capacity sitting empty; it excludes hyperscaler self-build. CRITICAL: a vacancy number is meaningless without its cause, and there are now THREE distinct causes in this dataset, DEMAND-TIGHT (Johor 0.7%: everything built is taken), POLICY-TIGHT (Singapore 4.9%: a regulatory moratorium caps supply, not a demand story), and ABSORPTION-LAG (Greater Manila 44%: operational capacity jumped 31% in six months and the new stock has not leased up yet, C&W expects it to ease). A red 44% cell does NOT mean nobody wants Manila.
meta.regions_note: Region is a rollup above country and is stored HERE ONLY, never on a facility row. Every facility already carries `country`, so writing a region onto each row would add no information and 240-plus chances to drift. The map reads this table to build the region tier of the scoreboard and the region switcher. Taxonomy calls on ambiguous countries get made once, in this object. `live: false` means the region is scaffolded but carries no facilities yet and must not be offered in the UI. CN added 2026-10-12 as a one-cluster pilot (Zhongwei, Ningxia), owner-approved in the scheduled build brief.

chip_controls.note: The Gulf analogue of what vacancy and grid queues are in Southeast Asia. What binds an AI data centre here is whether it can legally obtain US-controlled chips. This object holds the evidence. `chips.js` computes a per-project tier from it and never from judgment. READ THE SAMPLE SIZE HONESTLY: exactly three entities have a named, dated, government-sourced authorisation. That is enough for a categorical field and far too few for any MW-weighted percentage, so no rollup is computed or published. NOTE ON A CLAIM WE GOT WRONG EARLY: the framing that Gulf power is cheap does NOT hold for the UAE. Verified primary tariffs put Dubai near US$0.126/kWh, above every Southeast Asian market, and Abu Dhabi near US$0.074. Chips are still the harder constraint, and power is not the free variable it was assumed to be.

frameworks.note: Saudi Arabia was explicitly NOT included in the July 2026 UAE rule. It has no country-level framework and no approved-entity list. The distinction matters and is the sharpest fact in Gulf coverage. The UAE has a rule, Saudi Arabia has a licence.

frameworks.name: No US destination-based licence requirement as enforced

source.title: Supplement No. 1 to Part 740, Country Groups

frameworks.note: Country Group B on Supplement No. 1 to Part 740, not in D:1, D:4 or D:5. BIS enforces the destination-based licence requirement for advanced computing items only to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 (excluding A:5 and A:6), the October 2023 footprint, per its guidance of 2025-05-13 and 2026-05-31 and as restated in the UAE rule of 2026-07-14. The January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule text remains printed in the CFR, is not enforced, and has not been rescinded or replaced as of 2026-09-27. Exports to an entity headquartered in China or Macau, or whose ultimate parent is, still require a licence wherever the entity sits (15 CFR 744.23(a)(3) for .b items, 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) for .a items). Malaysia adds its own layer: since 2025-07-14 MITI requires a Strategic Trade Permit, with 30 days notice, for the export, transhipment and transit of US-origin high-performance AI chips under Section 12 of the Strategic Trade Act 2010, as an interim measure pending a Strategic Items List review. That governs chips leaving Malaysia, not chips arriving for use in a Malaysian data centre.

The January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule text remains printed in the CFR, is not enforced, and has not been rescinded or replaced as of 2026-09-27. Exports to an entity headquartered in China or Macau, or whose ultimate parent is, still require a licence wherever the entity sits (15 CFR 744.23(a)(3) for .b items, 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) for .a items). Singapore has prosecuted a fraud case (Aperia International, servers with Nvidia chips shipped on to Malaysia after Dell and Supermicro were deceived about the end user; fourth accused charged 2026-04-02). That is a diversion signal, not a licensing constraint on Singapore data centres.

chip_controls.approved_us_operators_note: Also named in Supplement No. 8 for the UAE. A UAE facility with one of these as a named operator or confirmed tenant has a structural reason to be compliant, which is why it earns the framework-covered tier rather than nothing. It is NOT evidence of a licence held by the facility's own operator and must never be read as one. In Saudi Arabia this signal does not apply at all, because there is no approved-entity list.
chip_controls.explicitly_undocumented_note: These entities appear constantly in trade press as Gulf AI infrastructure players and NONE has an export authorisation naming it in any government document found. Khazna is the important case. It is G42's colocation arm and has a public Nvidia infrastructure partnership, but a commercial partnership is not a licence and Khazna is not named in Supplement No. 8. Its access is inferred from corporate parentage only. Absence of a document is not evidence of denial, and the no-public-signal tier is a statement about the public record rather than about the company.

chip_controls.d5_headquartered_note: Entities headquartered in China or Macau, or whose ultimate parent is, as far as public ownership records show on 2026-09-27. chips.js grades a project licence_required_party when one of these is the operator, the operator's group, a funder, or a CONFIRMED client. Reported clients never trigger it. Rule: 15 CFR 744.23(a)(3) (.b items) and 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) (.a items); BIS guidance 2026-05-31 confirms the headquarters requirement is enforced even where the destination requirement is not. DayOne is deliberately absent: it was spun out of GDS International in 2024 and is Singapore-headquartered, so a GDS Holdings stake recorded as a funder on a row is what triggers the rule, never the DayOne name. Bridge Data Centres is caught only where a row names Chindata (its Beijing-headquartered parent, owned by Bain) in the operator name. Add or remove a name here because it is true of the ownership, never to move a tier.

OM.text: Oman was researched on 27 September 2026 and no data centre at or above 20MW IT load, and none with a confirmed hyperscaler or AI tenant, was found. Equinix MC1 and SN1 and Ooredoo's Salalah site are interconnection colo below the bar; Datamount Al Bandar publishes racks, not megawatts; Oman Data Park deployed Nvidia H200 GPUs with no site or capacity stated; Royal Decree 50/2026 created an AI Special Zone with no anchor project. Oman stays in scope and is rechecked at each Gulf refresh.
OM.checked_by: five-channel sweep (exchange disclosures, operator newsrooms, trade press, ministry releases, event coverage)

meta.checked_empty_note: Countries inside a live region that were researched and hold no row. Rendered as a muted line under the region on the map scoreboard, on the directory and on methodology.html, so a reader can tell 'checked and empty' from 'never looked'. The frontier five Southeast Asian countries are NOT here because nobody has looked yet.

cost_bands._about: Building cost benchmarks for the ArusGrid estimated value (2026-10-14, owner-approved). Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025, US$ per watt of IT load for an air-cooled 30-50MW hyperscale build, priced Oct 2024 to Oct 2025. Covers shell, fit-out and M&E with equipment; excludes land, utility works, site works, IT equipment and fees. Colocation or enterprise builds vary up to 15%; liquid cooling adds 7-10%. A country with no entry gets no estimate. Singapore is held: two reports of the same index print 14.53 and 15.43.

facilities.notes: MW BASIS IS MESSY. Jul 2024 (DCD, citing BDx site): 70MW live across 4,150 m2 white space, 'scalable up to 500MW'. Jun 2026 secondary coverage of the PLN deal says CGK4 delivers 'up to 650 MW'. BDx's own Jun 2026 PR only states 788 MVA of CONTRACTED GRID POWER (not IT load). Using 70MW live / 500MW planned IT (conservative, operator-sourced); flag the 650MW figure as unverified and the 788MVA as grid, not IT. JV: BDx + Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison + Lintasarta; the JV bought Indosat's DC portfolio in 2024. [verify 2026-07-13] Treat 70MW as reported/design capacity, not verified live IT load: 70MW over 4,150 sqm white space = ~17kW/m2, implausible for a 75-day phase-1 build; DCD itself hedges the figure. [audit 2026-07-13 - CEILING vs COMMITTED] Three numbers reconcile as ONE: 788 MVA contracted grid (PLN, Jun 2026) ~ 630MW at unity ~ the 'designed to deliver up to 650MW' claim. i.e. 650 TRACKS THE GRID FEED, not IT load - the same number wearing different clothes. The 2024 '500MW scalable' figure is superseded by 650. The only figure with a build behind it is 70MW LIVE. Honest reading: ~70MW built, a 650MW/788MVA envelope, and no committed IT-load figure in between. Our planned_mw of 500 is a DESIGN CEILING, not a commitment (rule 12) - flag for the next eval. AI status is unambiguous: Indonesia's first NVIDIA DGX-Ready-certified campus, H100-class deployments, up to 120kW/rack with liquid cooling. [refresh 2026-09-26] BDx broke ground on 'AI Campus 2 (CGK4)' at Jatiluhur on 2026-09-22. Building 1 of 6 is 120MW IT in phases, first contracted phase operational early 2027. The 640MW campus figure is not stated as IT load and sits beside 845MVA of secured grid, so planned_mw stays 500 (rule 2). The groundbreaking also sharpens the doubt on the 70MW live figure: if the campus needed a first-building groundbreaking in 2026, the 2024 '70MW live' was probably design capacity at an earlier hall. Re-verify at the next eval. [verified 2026-09-26] LIVE 70 -> null, PLANNED 500 -> 120 (rules 9 and 12). BDx's own 2024 launch release gives no MW for phase 1 ('deployed within a record time of 75 days'); the 70MW exists only in DCD's write-up and is not credible as IT load (~17kW/sqm). AI Campus 2 is BDx's new name for the same CGK4 site. The only committed IT figure is Building 1 at 120MW, first phase early 2027. 500, 640 and 650 are ceilings tracking the 788 to 845MVA grid envelope and live in notes. Promote further buildings only on a dated commitment. [2026-10-05] West Java's governor asked BDx on 2026-09-30 to halt work at Jatiluhur one week after the 22 Sep groundbreaking because the AMDAL environmental approval and the PBG building permit had not been issued (TechNode). Building 1 of 6 (120MW IT, first contracted phase early 2027) therefore has a ceremony but no permitted construction on record; its phase is held at land_permitting until BDx or the province reports the permits issued and work resumed. The 640MW campus figure is not stated as IT load; 845 MVA is grid. [2026-10-10] Stage expanding to on_hold, dated 2026-09-30. West Java governor Dedi Mulyadi halted construction at Jatiluhur because the AMDAL and the PBG building permit were not issued (Investor Trust 2026-10-02, TechNode 2026-09-30). Bisnis (2026-10-05) reports that the 5 Oct ANDAL session reached no decision. The existing 2026-09-22 stage_history entry records the groundbreaking, which happened; the halt shows work had begun, so the 2026-10-05 reading that Building 1 had no construction is superseded and the building phase is now on_hold rather than land_permitting. The whole row is on_hold because its only planned MW is Building 1 (120MW IT, first phase early 2027 before the halt). The 2024 phase-one GPU Merdeka plant is not reported as affected and stays operational in phases. 640MW is a campus figure with no IT basis; PLN 845MVA is grid. Return the row to expanding when the permits issue and work resumes, with a dated source. The groundbreaking took place on 22 Sep 2026 with the governor and regent present (Bisnis). Building 1 is 120MW IT. The 640MW campus figure has no stated basis and stays out of planned MW. No resumption after the halt was reported by 8 Oct 2026 (Selular.id). [2026-10-16] On 30 Sep 2026 Minister Airlangga said he had received no communication from West Java about a delay (Bisnis, 2026-10-01). Stage stays on hold until a resumption source exists. STT GDC PH says it runs SEVEN PH data centres totalling ~150MW IT — that reconciles as Fairview (124 planned) + a legacy estate of ~26MW across six sub-20MW sites (correctly excluded by the bar). STT GDC PH's '>140MW across 7 DCs' claim is a MARKETING CEILING (rule 12), now fully reconciled: Fairview 124MW ultimate build (four buildings — corroborated independently by PCIJ, 11 Jan 2026) + STT Cavite 1 & 2 (6MW total IT, Cavite 2 in testing/commissioning Apr 2026) + Makati + Davao. There is NO hidden large Cavite expansion — that watchlist item is CLOSED. Fairview 1 and Cavite are both covered by a 10-yr renewable supply agreement with MPower (Meralco's retail arm). [GAP CLOSED 2026-07-13] The 'STT runs 7 PH data centers / ~150MW' statement is RECONCILED and there is NO hidden capacity: 27.2MW legacy estate (5 sites carved out of Globe: Quezon City 5.5, Cavite 4.8, Makati 3.0, + Davao + a third Manila site, incl. a 5.2MW expansion) + STT Cavite 2 (6MW) + Fairview's 124MW DESIGN ceiling = ~157MW. The 150MW is a full-build design figure, not built capacity. Independent proof: DICT puts the ENTIRE country below 200MW today - STT alone cannot be 150MW live. Operator-stated Fairview build-out (CEO Carlomagno Malana, BusinessWorld 23 Apr 2026): 28MW today -> 32MW by end-2026; Fairview 2 adds a further 32MW, still IN DESIGN, completion targeted late-2026/early-2027, halls deploying over 18-24 months after. So COMMITTED near-term = 64MW; 124MW is the scalable design ceiling (rule 12 - read the pipeline accordingly). The Philstar 'STT Cavite undergoing testing and commissioning' lead resolves to STT Cavite 2 (6MW, sub-bar). WATCHLIST: STT is scouting Visayas and says it has a Mindanao site beyond Davao. [refresh 2026-08-28] EXPANDING FROM 28MW TO 32MW BY END-2026 per STT GDC Philippines, against the 124MW ultimate build phased to demand. Live MW stays at 28 until a post-event source confirms the 32. FLAGGED CONFLICT, NOT RESOLVED: STT GDC was reported at nearly 150MW combined Philippine IT load in Apr 2026 and at 128MW in Aug 2026 for the same seven facilities. Neither figure is reconciled and neither overrides our per-facility numbers. [refresh 2026-09-11] LIVE 32MW, 2026-08. InsiderPH (2026-08-04) reports STT GDC 'recently energized 32 MW of capacity at its flagship Philippine campus', which closes the +4MW phase the CEO had targeted for end-2026 (BusinessWorld, Apr 2026). The 128MW figure is the seven-facility national total and is consistent with the Aug figure already noted. Campus stage question for the lead: with Fairview 1 complete and Fairview 2 carried as announced, the campus no longer has a building phase, so by the rule used for A-FLOW the stage would be operational rather than expanding. The CEO's Apr-2026 statement that Fairview 2 is 'targeted for completion by late this year or early next year' implies works underway but does not say so. Hold expanding only if the lead accepts that inference; otherwise set operational. LEAD DECISION: stage set to operational because Fairview 1 is built out and Fairview 2 has no construction source; it returns to expanding when one appears. [refresh 2026-09-11] Ownership changed 2026-09-01: the KKR-led consortium (KKR 75%, Singtel 25%) completed its purchase of STT GDC; ST Telemedia and Temasek exit at platform level. [refresh 2026-09-13] 2026-08-10. Manila Bulletin, citing Globe, describes Fairview by floor. Level 1 halls reached full capacity in H1 2026, Level 2 is 'under commissioning', Levels 3 and 4 are in design, 124MW at completion. Globe CEO Carl Cruz says the JV is 'having a hard time keeping up with the influx of orders'. This is a floor description of the first building and does not say Fairview 2 construction has started, so the operational stage set on 2026-09-11 stands. If Level 2 is additional to the 32MW energised in August, live MW will move again; no MW is attached to the floors.

facilities.notes: STALLED / ZOMBIE — correctly frozen at land_permitting, but DO NOT COUNT ITS 300MW IN ANY CREDIBLE PIPELINE. Verified 2026-07-13. LATEST DATED SOURCE OF ANY KIND: 11-12 Jun 2024 — 25 MONTHS AGO. WHAT EXISTS: a signed 50-year lease with the Tarlac provincial government over 47ha of BCDA land (60/40 revenue split). THAT IS ALL. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: groundbreaking (it was SCHEDULED for Aug 2024 — no post-event source anywhere), EPC contractor, funder, PPA, anchor tenant, financial close. The sponsor's own Phase-1 targets (Q4 2025, then Q4 2026) have both blown. WHO IS ENDEC: a Manila design-build/consulting-engineering firm whose stated track record is water systems, blending plants, schools, diagnostic labs and helipads — no DC track record, no disclosed balance sheet, no capital partner for a US$2.7B build. The project originated at a 2023 Marcos investment roundtable — pipeline-inflation provenance. THE LANDLORD'S SILENCE IS THE KILLER: BCDA has published nothing on Narra since the 2024 lease, and skipped it in TWO 2026 announcements that would have named a live 300MW anchor (the 20 Apr 2026 Pax Silica AI-hub allocation of 4,000 acres in New Clark City, and the 3 Jul 2026 FAILURE OF BIDDING on NCC's P2.5B fibre backbone — zero bidders, third failed attempt since 2023, so NCC has no committed fibre backbone). Meralco's own white paper notes 99% of PH hyperscale investment chooses Meralco franchise areas and names New Clark City as OUTSIDE it. No cancellation source exists, so it is not cancellable on evidence — but it is not creditable either. [STAGE 2026-07-13: land_permitting -> on_hold] Every retrievable source dates from June 2024 (the lease signing). Searched 2025-26 for construction, EPC award, financing, PPA, groundbreaking AND for stall/shelve language: NOTHING EXISTS IN EITHER DIRECTION. Two years of total silence on a US$2.7B project. The Aug-2024 groundbreaking was SCHEDULED and never confirmed by any post-event source (rule 8). Phase-1 RFS has silently slipped Q4 2025 -> Q4 2026 across retellings with no sponsor statement doing the slipping. No EPC, no named funder, no PPA, no utility corroboration - and the site is OUTSIDE the Meralco franchise, so the PH utility discovery channel (rule 14) structurally cannot corroborate it. The 300MW is a 3x100MW CONCEPT on a land lease: the largest number in the PH pipeline resting on the thinnest evidence in the dataset. Not cancelled - no source says it died. [audit 2026-08-18] BCDA's president said in early Aug 2026 that no AI or hyperscale data centers will rise in New Clark City, citing power and water limits, and that a US hyperscale investor chose Malaysia instead. The landlord has publicly ruled out the category on this land. [refresh 2026-08-28] MOVED TO CANCELLED. The landlord has now ruled out the use case in public. BCDA president Joshua Bingcang stated on 2026-08-11 that large AI and hyperscale data centers will not locate at New Clark City because electricity supply is insufficient, and BOI managing head Ceferino Rodolfo said at the same briefing that no AI company will build and operate a data processing center there. NCC's designated tech hub is now defined as AI component manufacturing rather than compute. Corroborating: the P2.5B NCC fibre backbone joint-venture tender failed for a third time (notice 2026-06-25, public 2026-07-03) after zero bidding documents were submitted across a 13-month window, so the site has no committed backbone. Against 26 months of silence, no EPC, no funder, no PPA and no financial close, this is a stronger cancellation basis than most projects in the graveyard carry. Its 300MW was already excluded from credible pipeline and is now excluded from every total. [refresh 2026-09-11] CORROBORATION, 2026-09-11. BCDA's own clarification (PIA, 2026-08-10) says the Pax Silica hub at New Clark City will host semiconductor and advanced manufacturing 'rather than a data processing center', with dedicated off-grid generation for that use. Philstar (2026-09-03) restates the hub as 1,620 ha with contract negotiations in 2026, planning 2027 and construction from early 2028. Watch for confusion: some Pax Silica coverage (Philstar, 2026-07-24) lists data centres among possible tenants. The landlord's on-record position remains that hyperscale data centres will not locate at NCC.

fate.summary: Only a land lease ever existed. No builder, funder, power deal or tenant appeared in over two years, the sponsor had no data center record, and the landlord left it out of its own 2026 announcements.

THE DETAILS NEVER CAME. No partner was ever named; no site work, permit, capex line or follow-up article in 38 months. DECISIVE: Converge has since enumerated its own estate and pipeline WITHOUT IT — Manila Bulletin, 20 Mar 2026 lists its four DCs (Angeles 12MW, Caloocan 3MW, Pasig, Clark, ~20MW combined) and its forward pipeline (a Batangas prospective site, possible Visayas/Mindanao), with no Paranaque anywhere; CEO of Converge Studios: 'we will not fight yet in the megawatt race'. facilities.notes: A Xinhua dispatch dated 16 Jul 2026 says construction began recently. Both phases are being built at once, with a target of delivery and power-on by end 2026. Phase 1 is 3.6 billion yuan and phase 2 is 1.5 billion yuan. The phase 1 EPC tender carried an estimate of about 3.675 billion yuan. A China Construction Sixth Engineering Bureau consortium was the first-ranked candidate in July 2026, which is a preliminary result and not a final award. Xinhua Finance (Sep 2026) says the client needs racks by end of October. Compute targets are 108,000 P for phase 1 and 136,000 P in total. These are notes only. No MW figure is published. [2026-10-14] Under_construction from 2026-07-16 is right. Xinhua (dateline Lanzhou 2026-07-16, republished 2026-07-20) says phase 1 formally started construction 'recently' (近日) at the Qingyang 东数西算 park. The China News Service piece of 2026-08-02 does NOT say works had not started: its sentence '项目还没开工，算力就已经全部被预订一空了' means the compute was fully pre-booked before construction began; the same paragraph has the project head standing at a busy worksite (工地边…忙碌的场面) with civil and M&E works due for joint delivery on 30 Oct. The CNS piece is the newest dated source and it supports active construction. The EPC tender (bidder 智创蓝图数字科技（甘肃）有限公司) planned a 2026-07-05 start and 300 calendar days to 2027-05-01. Both media sources spell the project 智慧蓝图; the tendering company is 智创蓝图. Xinhua's exact start day is not given, so the 2026-07-16 date is the dateline, not a stated ground-breaking day. No new stage_history op. (中国新闻网, 2026-08-02) [2026-10-15] Phase 1 started in July 2026 with CNY 3.6bn for 3 data halls and 8,860 racks of 15 to 50kW. Phase 2 adds CNY 1.5bn and 2,215 high-density racks. Total CNY 5.1bn (about USD 718m) and 136,000P. Both phases are built together with year-end delivery targeted. (凤凰网 (Xinhua), 2026-07-20) [2026-10-16] Press (2026-07-09) reports 250MW of contracted IT load from three clients. Contracted load is not built capacity, so planned MW stays blank. [2026-10-17] Xinhua Finance (2026-09-10) says piling is under way on phase 1 to meet a client deadline at the end of October 2026, and gives phase 1 as three buildings with about 108,000P of compute. [2026-10-17 15:08] The 2026-07-09 China.com report states that phase 1 正式开工 (formally started) in the Qingyang East Data West Computing park, with phases 1 and 2 built together. With the Xinhua dispatch of 2026-07-16 this supports the under_construction stage. The chinanews line of 2026-08-02 that the project had not started is the outlier.

Two-year term with six months of exclusivity; the principal commercial terms are non-binding. Scope is feasibility: site, power, cooling, permitting, demand and financing. BTC Digital says it will decide on investment or construction only after these are validated. planned_mw DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the 300MW and 200ha in coverage are the industrial park's planned power load and land area, not the data center's (DCD says BTC Digital has not disclosed data center capacity and the MoU has no power supply agreement). Some project databases attribute 300MW and 200ha to the data center itself; that is the park. The park's infrastructure (developer Vinhomes Industrial Park Investment JSC, over 200ha, VND 2,252bn) broke ground 14 May 2026. No approvals reported. Held 2026-10-13 as non-binding; added 2026-10-14 for consistency with comparable MoU-stage rows (e.g. SAIGONTEL Nam Tan Tap).

facilities.notes: A Guohai Securities note (2026-10-12) says that by the 2026 interim report the Ulanqab 496.8MW green intelligent computing centre had approval from the Ulanqab Development and Reform Commission, with preliminary procedures, power supply and financing in progress. Jinkai signed with Ulanqab on 10 Feb 2026 alongside China Unicom, Boda Data and one other firm; those four projects total about 1,600MW of IT load and about 285,000 racks combined, with no split by project. The district is not published, so coordinates are at city level. [2026-10-17] The approval named in the H1 2026 report is a two-high (high energy use, high emissions) project assessment opinion. Ulanqab DRC issued it jointly with three other departments under document 乌发改环资字〔2026〕392号. It is not a project filing. At the 2026-09-23 results briefing the company said pre-construction procedures, technical plan, power supply and financing were still in progress. It gave no start date and would not say whether the project has customers. No investment, IT load, racks or district were disclosed. (Stockstar (company announcement), 2026-09-23)
